page: Amazon Web Services r6id.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at up to 3.5 GHz. The server offers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, paired with 128 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3000 MHz. This creates an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also includes 950 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, while operating without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results place the r6id.4xlarge consistently in the middle tiers for general x86 compute and memory throughput. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1650.0 and a multi-core score of 9796.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 21005.41. Memory bandwidth reaches 97.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 57.64 GB/sec for writes. For database-centric benchmarks, it handles 15.88 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 7564.77 on PassMark database operations, benefiting directly from high memory density and AVX-512 vector support.

The presence of 950 GB of dedicated local NVMe storage offers substantial I/O benefits for transient scratch data, write-heavy caching, and temporary database tables compared to purely network-attached EBS volumes. However, as an ephemeral store, data does not persist across instance stops, requiring structured replication strategies. The instance exhibits weak throughput on 7B LLM prompt processing (31.86 tokens/sec), emphasizing that heavy tensor operations require dedicated accelerators rather than CPU execution.

With its 128 GB memory capacity and high-speed local NVMe disk, the r6id.4xlarge provides a balanced hardware cost-efficiency profile for in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, caching layers like Redis or Memcached, and large relational database servers requiring fast local swap or scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services r6id.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor with 16 vCPUs and 8 physical cores running at 3.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro architecture. It features 128 GB of DDR4 RAM, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for memory-intensive workloads. In addition to a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the configuration bundles a 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance store for low-latency scratch space and caching. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the middle 50% tier, achieving 15.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 97.52 GB/sec in large-block read memory bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPUs, it is unsuited for heavy AI training, but its hardware configuration fits production relational databases, in-memory caches, search indexes, and distributed analytics pipelines.
